Moga (modern girl) dressed in beach pajamas style walking through the streets of Ginza in 1928

Unfortunately, I can't edit the title. I meant Beach Pajamas, a type of clothing popular in the 1920s to 1930s.

The Japanese moga or "modern girl" were basically the Japanese equivalent of flappers in the 1920s. They were Japanese women who sported Western clothing and ideas. They were financially independent, went to cafes, participated in casual sex and completely defied traditional gender roles.

However, they were likely largely a media creation, who viewed mogas through "Japanese vs Westernization" lens. The media critiqued the rapid Westernization occurring throughout Japan during and before the Taisho era, mogas being an example of what happens when the West meets Japan.

This was also post-Great Kanto Earthquake, which can be a fairly strong marker for a sudden shift in the Japanese view of Westernization/Modernization. Furthermore, not long after the Great Kanto Earthquake, the Taisho period came to an end, replaced with the Showa. Moga similarly didn't last long. After the 1920s, the reversion to more "traditional" society saw the return of the "good wife, good mother" view of women.

More information on the Taisho period and modernity.
